_comment: Data retention / TTL windows. Read by services/cart_ttl.py (cart-age labels) and the retention
DELIBERATE DESIGN DECISION — retention is UNIFORM across every user. It is NOT gated on IP, GeoIP,
ASN, or inferred country. GDPR scope is set by where the controller is established and by the
targeting test (Art. 3), NOT by a request's IP geolocation: an EU resident is protected whether they
connect from Paris or Bali, and a VPN egress in Frankfurt does not make a non-EU person an EU data
subject. IP-geo gating would under-protect travelling/VPN'd EU users, over-apply to non-EU users on
EU exits, and — worst — force us to process MORE personal data (IP/ASN/geo) just to decide who gets
privacy. So: one policy for everyone. Do not add a geo gate here.
The on-demand right-to-erasure (Art. 17) is a SEPARATE mechanism — see routers/privacy.py
erasure serves the right to be forgotten. Keep both; they are not substitutes.
Windows below are engineering defaults and want legal/counsel sign-off before they are treated as
final. They are configurable so that is a one-line change.
